oceanic crust less than ∼ 1 million years old was subducted in Palawan, the Philippines.
oceanic spreading center lithosphere is a preferred site of subduction nucleation and that the process of subduction initiation can be rapid.
a divergent boundary was forcefully and rapidly converted into a subduction zone, that the subduction initiation site was a young spreading center, and that the process was rapid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how subduction zones form.
how subduction zones form and the dynamics of the plate boundary that precedes subduction.
the tectonic processes that occur at the beginning of plate tectonics, when the oceanic crust is still young and buoyant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a divergent boundary was forcefully and rapidly converted to a convergent boundary.
the rapid conversion of a divergent boundary into a subduction zone occurred in the western Philippines.
subduction initiation is not a single, simple process but rather a combination of several different mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

subduction initiation is a process of forcing a weak plate boundary to subduct, and this process may occur repeatedly at a spreading center until the plate is sufficiently dense and old to subduct by itself.
the oceanic lithosphere that is formed at the spreading center is weak and can be subducted, but it takes a lot of energy and time.
a rapid change in plate motion from divergence to convergence occurred along a spreading center.
The main takeaway from our work is that
buoyant, weak lithosphere can be forced to subduct.
the buoyant, but relatively weak, oceanic lithosphere of a spreading center was forced to underthrust a denser, older oceanic lithosphere.
subduction initiation can occur at a divergent plate margin and that the lithosphere at a divergent margin is sufficiently weak and buoyant to be forced into subduction.
